preconditions.expression: all(1 <= int(x) <= 10**5 for line in stdin.splitlines() for x in line.split() if x.isdigit())
preconditions.description: All integers in input are within bounds 1 ≤ n ≤ 10^5, 0 ≤ m ≤ 10^5, and 1 ≤ k ≤ 10^9.
Input has exactly m + 1 lines: first line with n, m, k; followed by m lines of clue links.
Each of the m link lines contains exactly two integers.

preconditions.expression: all(int(a) != int(b) for line in stdin.splitlines()[1:] for a, b in [line.split()])
preconditions.description: No direct link connects a clue to itself.

preconditions.expression: all((a, b) != (b, a) or i == j for i, line_i in enumerate(stdin.splitlines()[1:]) for j, line_j in enumerate(stdin.splitlines()[1:]) for a, b in [line_i.split()] for c, d in [line_j.split()])
preconditions.description: No duplicate direct links exist between the same pair of clues (order does not matter).

postconditions.description: Output is a non-negative integer less than k, representing the number of ways modulo k.

postconditions.expression: all(1 <= int(x) <= n for line in stdin.splitlines()[1:] for x in line.split())
postconditions.description: All clue IDs in links are valid (1 ≤ clue ID ≤ n).
T is the minimum number of additional direct links needed to make the graph connected, where T = (n choose 2) - m (total possible edges minus existing edges).

postconditions.expression: stdout == str(compute_ways(n, m, k, parse_links(stdin))) % k
postconditions.description: Output is the number of ways to add exactly T edges to the existing graph such that the resulting graph is connected, modulo k. The function compute_ways(n, m, k, links) is defined as the number of spanning trees of the complete graph minus the existing edges, multiplied by the number of ways to add exactly T edges to make the graph connected.
